study_design: Prospective Netherlands Cohort Study with multivariate case-cohort analyses
cohort_total_n_excerpt: The association between 21 vegetables and eight fruits and prostate cancer risk was assessed in the Netherlands Cohort Study among 58,279 men of ages 55-69 years at baseline in 1986.
reason: The abstract analyzes prostate cancer risk overall. Its unspecified subgroup analyses do not establish an aggressive incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Observed positive associations were significant for consumption of leek (RR, 1.38) and oranges (RR, 1.07) and nonsignificant for sweet peppers (RR, 1.60) and mushrooms (RR, 1.49).
estimate_classifications.reason: The sweet-pepper estimate concerns overall prostate cancer risk. The abstract describes individual vegetables as continuous variables rather than supporting the row's imputed high-versus-low comparison, but the endpoint remains general.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: For vegetables categorized in botanical groups, no associations were found except for consumption of pulses (RR, 0.71; CI, 0.51-0.98; P for trend, 0.01).
estimate_classifications.reason: The pulses/legumes estimate is for overall prostate cancer risk, not an aggressive incident subtype.

validation_findings: Nested case-control/case-cohort analytic denominator must not be forced to full-cohort N
